prompt.context: Your client is a national drug-store that is adding a new type of hair dye to its retail offering. 'Highlights Dye' allows customers to comb in small amounts of various colors to hair rather than the traditional method of dyeing the whole head. The client is considering launching its own in-house brand or carrying an existing recognized brand-name called 'Vibrants'.
prompt.question: Should the drugstore carry Vibrants over its in-store brand?

clarifying_info.q: Does the chain already have an in-house brand for other products?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, the retail chain already carries its in-house brand in many products (toothpaste, cotton swabs, etc.) including traditional hair dye in both temporary and permanent varieties.
It is a fashion-forward product available in natural and fluorescent colors. Each application lasts roughly 30 days.
The target customer is under 30 years of age.

clarifying_info.q: What is the primary business objective?

exhibits.title: Pricing Considerations
exhibits.shows: A table comparing retail and wholesale prices for the In-House Brand and Vibrants, with footnotes about pricing constraints and market size.

data.Note 1: If selling Vibrants, the drugstore cannot change the retail price or run price promotions on the product.

exhibits.title: Sample Focus Group Answers
exhibits.shows: A table of focus group respondents showing Gender, Age, and Answer (Y/N) to the question: 'Would you purchase a store-brand version of Vibrants over the brand name?'

framework: Product attributes: application length (temporary ~30 days vs. permanent), color varieties (natural vs. fluorescent), application process (home vs. salon), ingredients (chemical vs. natural dye), packaging/branding
Market & customer: identify target demographic (fashion-conscious under-30s, natural/aging customers covering grey hair, DIYers avoiding salon prices); assess market trends and competitive landscape
Financials: compare unit margins for Vibrants vs. in-house brand; calculate profit at anticipated market size; assess pricing flexibility and promotional restrictions
Capabilities & launch feasibility: R&D, manufacturing, packaging, and promotion costs needed to develop an in-house highlights product; impact on 90-day timeline
Opportunity costs & cannibalization: risk of the new product cannibalizing existing in-house hair dye sales

questions.prompt: Calculate the profit margin (per unit) for the In-House Brand and for Vibrants. Which has the higher margin?
questions.guidance: Candidate should use the per-1,000-unit figures and convert to per-unit for clarity. In-House Brand: margin = retail minus wholesale = $5,000 - $2,000 = $3,000 per 1,000 units = $3.00/unit (60% margin). Vibrants: margin = $6,500 - $4,500 = $2,000 per 1,000 units = $2.00/unit (31% margin). Conclusion: In-House Brand has a superior margin ($3 vs $2 per unit).

math.setup: Margin per 1,000 units = Retail price - Wholesale price. Prices are per 1,000 units.
steps: In-House Brand margin = $5,000 - $2,000 = $3,000 per 1,000 units = $3.00 per unit
Vibrants margin = $6,500 - $4,500 = $2,000 per 1,000 units = $2.00 per unit
math.answer: In-House Brand margin: $3.00/unit (60%). Vibrants margin: $2.00/unit (31%). The In-House Brand has a higher absolute and percentage margin.

questions.prompt: Using the focus group data (Exhibit 2), what proportion of under-30 respondents would purchase the store-brand version? What about over-30 respondents? What does this imply?
questions.guidance: Candidate should segment by age and note the question is phrased inversely — 'Yes' means willingness to buy the in-store brand, NOT Vibrants. Under 30 (8 respondents: ages 29, 27, 24, 25, 29, 26, 23, 28): only 1 answered Y (age 24) = 12.5% would buy in-store brand, meaning 87.5% prefer Vibrants. Over 30 (3 respondents: ages 33, 31, 31): all 3 answered Y = 100% would buy in-store brand. Main insight: the target customer segment (under 30) overwhelmingly prefers the Vibrants brand-name over the in-store alternative. A strong candidate may flag the small sample size; if asked, confirm it is representative of a larger study.

math.setup: Count Y responses by age group. Note: Y = willing to purchase store-brand (i.e., does NOT prefer Vibrants).
steps: Under-30 respondents: F29-N, F27-N, F24-Y, M25-N, F29-N, F26-N, F23-N, F28-N → 1 Y out of 8 = 12.5% would buy store brand; 87.5% prefer Vibrants
Over-30 respondents: M33-Y, M31-Y, M31-Y → 3 Y out of 3 = 100% would buy store brand
math.answer: Under-30: 12.5% willing to buy store brand (87.5% prefer Vibrants). Over-30: 100% willing to buy store brand.

questions.prompt: Given the financial and customer data, what is the overall recommendation? Should the drugstore carry Vibrants?
questions.guidance: Candidate should synthesize: despite the In-House Brand having superior margins, the target customer (under 30) is overwhelmingly unwilling to purchase the store-brand alternative. Carrying only the in-house brand risks very low uptake from the intended market. An excellent candidate will also cite the 90-day launch timeline as a reason to carry Vibrants — developing an in-house highlights dye requires R&D, manufacturing, packaging, and promotion that cannot realistically be completed in 90 days.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the risks and next steps if the drugstore decides to carry Vibrants?

categories.name: Risks
ideas: Trend/demand risk: Highlights Dye is fashion-forward; consumer demand could decline quickly, especially given the under-30 target demographic
Pricing inflexibility: the drugstore cannot change the retail price or run promotions on Vibrants, limiting competitive response
Lower margins vs. in-house brand reduce overall profitability per unit sold
Brand dependency: reliance on an external brand means the drugstore has no control over product quality, supply, or brand perception
Cannibalization: Vibrants could cannibalize existing in-house traditional hair dye sales

categories.name: Next Steps
ideas: Develop a marketing and promotional plan targeting the under-30 demographic
Procure initial orders and negotiate favorable wholesale terms with Vibrants
Plan shelf-space allocation and in-store placement strategy
Monitor sales performance and trend data with a 90-day review
Evaluate long-term option to develop an in-house highlights dye once market demand is validated

recommendation: The drugstore should carry Vibrants rather than attempting to launch its own in-house Highlights Dye brand at this time.

Although the in-house brand would generate higher margins ($3.00/unit vs. $2.00/unit), the target customer segment (under 30) overwhelmingly prefers the Vibrants brand name — only 12.5% would purchase an in-store alternative.
Additionally, the 90-day launch timeline makes developing a new in-house product infeasible given the R&D, manufacturing, packaging, and promotion requirements.
risks: Demand risk: the fashion-forward nature of the product means consumer interest may decline rapidly
Pricing inflexibility: the drugstore cannot discount or promote Vibrants, limiting its competitive flexibility
next_steps: Develop a targeted marketing plan for the under-30 demographic
Procure initial orders and plan shelf-space allocation
Revisit the in-house brand option once market demand is validated and timeline constraints ease
